title: What to eat
intro: Andorran cooking is Pyrenean mountain food: escudella (a pork-and-vegetable stew, traditionally a winter dish — exactly in season for a November trip) and trinxat (mashed cabbage and potato, pan-fried hard with cured pork) show up on most traditional menus once the weather turns cold. A borda — literally a mountain barn, now shorthand for a stone-walled grill restaurant — is the classic way to eat both. Beyond the two picks below, the Barri Antic's cluster of casual tapas bars and old-town restaurants around Carrer Major covers the rest of the trip's meals without booking ahead.

items.name: MiraKbé
items.area: Carrer Pere d'Urg, Andorra la Vella — off the touristy Avinguda Meritxell shopping street
items.address: Carrer Pere d'Urg 10, AD500 Andorra la Vella
items.hours: 10:00–16:00 & 19:00–23:00 Mon–Sat, closed Sundays; weekday lunch set menu 13:00–15:15
items.how: ≈5-minute walk from the Barri Antic; à la carte tapas at dinner
items.crowd_tip: Two independent accounts — a food blog and a diner review — point here instead of Andorra la Vella's touristier Avinguda Meritxell restaurants, citing better value and quality.
items.why: A gastrobar two independent reviewers single out over the pricier spots on Avinguda Meritxell.

items.name: Borda Estevet
items.area: Carretera de la Comella, just outside central Andorra la Vella
items.address: Ctra. de la Comella i de la Plana, 2, AD500 Andorra la Vella
items.how: ≈10-minute walk or short taxi from the Barri Antic
items.why: A 250-seat converted stone barn built around a wood-fired grill — the classic borda experience within easy reach of the capital.
